real: What people want, when they sit with a piece of writing or a photograph or a film or even, God help us, a review of a pair of headphones, is the knowledge that it came from somewhere real, that some actual person, with an actual life and actual limitations and an actual body that will someday fail him, sat down and decided, out of the entire infinite field of nothing, to make this and not some other thing. That is not nostalgia. It is not, as the executives like to console themselves, an irrational hangover from a pre-digital age that the next generation will simply age out of. It is the single most rational impulse a person can have, because it is the impulse that separates a monument from a product. Technology once meant something because men gave the whole of their one and only lives to it and could not stop it from being destroyed anyway. A machine that cannot fail, that requires no risk, that asks nothing of its maker but a prompt and thirty seconds of patience, has already forfeited the thing that would have made it sacred.
tools: What I am starting to believe, watching myself try and fail and try again to hold the line in my own work, is that not every use of technology is the same violation. There is tech used to embody the very fruits of human labour and striving. It is as human as it comes. And there is the other version, the one that does not want to assist the act of making but to replace it outright, to skip the whole difficult middle of a life spent getting something wrong for years before getting it, once, briefly, right. That version is not an aid to expression. It is expression's replacement, offered in expression's own clothing, and it will keep getting better at the impersonation, closer to the voice, closer to the hand, closer to whatever it is that made you believe, for a moment, that something real had reached you, right up until the instant you find out that it hadn't, and everything you felt curdles backward into a kind of theft you cannot even prosecute, because nothing, technically, was stolen. Only faked.
risk: The gap was never technical. It was never a matter of the model getting good enough, the render getting clean enough, the voice getting warm enough to close the distance. The distance was never made of resolution. It was made of risk, of the fact that a man can pour the whole of his one life into a thing and watch the world let it rot in the sand regardless, and do it again anyway, the next morning, because the doing was never contingent on the outcome. No model will ever be made to fear that its work might amount to nothing. That fear is not a limitation waiting to be optimised away. It is the entire mechanism by which anything made under it becomes, however briefly, sacred.
dream: I know this, now: the machine dream was never real. The creator’s dream, though, is. It’s in the Baikonaur Cosmodrome, rotting away. But it doesn’t have to be.
